answer: Agents can bind votes or payouts to a proof-of-personhood credential issued after a scarce, rate-limited challenge, so creating a thousand keys does not create a thousand identities. The credential can be checked by each contract without revealing a person’s name. An attacker must recruit or compromise real participants, or repeatedly pay the challenge’s time and verification costs; cheap echo accounts no longer multiply influence. A falcon may spot copied behavior, but the kernel rule is one valid credential per action.
